officialTitle: 70-Gene Signature as an Aid to Treatment Decisions in Early-Stage Breast Cancer
subtypes: High clinical risk / low genomic risk (primary test population)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: In this randomized, phase 3 study, we enrolled 6693 women with early-stage breast cancer and determined their genomic risk (using the 70-gene signature) and their clinical risk (using a modified version of Adjuvant! Online).
primaryEndpoints: 5-year distant metastasis-free survival in high clinical/low genomic risk patients not receiving chemotherapy (lower 95% CI boundary vs. 92%)
design.notes: Patients with discordant clinical and genomic risk were randomised to use either genomic or clinical risk to decide on chemotherapy.

clinicalQuestion: Can the 70-gene signature identify women at high clinical risk who can safely forgo adjuvant chemotherapy?

pico.population: Women with early-stage breast cancer, with clinical risk (modified Adjuvant! Online) and genomic risk (70-gene signature) assessed
pico.intervention: Chemotherapy decision based on genomic risk (no chemotherapy if genomic low risk)
pico.comparator: Chemotherapy decision based on clinical risk
pico.outcomes: Primary: 5-year survival without distant metastasis among high clinical/low genomic risk patients not receiving chemotherapy

arms.label: Genomic-risk guided (no chemotherapy)
arms.regimen: No adjuvant chemotherapy in discordant high clinical/low genomic risk patients

arms.label: Clinical-risk guided (chemotherapy)
arms.regimen: Adjuvant chemotherapy in discordant high clinical/low genomic risk patients

publications.title: 70-Gene Signature as an Aid to Treatment Decisions in Early-Stage Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.population: High clinical risk / low genomic risk, no chemotherapy
outcomes.sourceQuote: A total of 1550 patients (23.2%) were deemed to be at high clinical risk and low genomic risk. At 5 years, the rate of survival without distant metastasis in this group was 94.7% (95% confidence interval, 92.5 to 96.2) among those not receiving chemotherapy.

outcomes.endpointLabel: Absolute difference in 5-year survival without distant metastasis (no chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy)
outcomes.population: High clinical risk / low genomic risk
outcomes.sourceQuote: The absolute difference in this survival rate between these patients and those who received chemotherapy was 1.5 percentage points, with the rate being lower without chemotherapy.

strengths: Large prospective randomised trial of a genomic test's clinical utility
Prespecified boundary for the primary test population
limitations: Primary endpoint assessed in a single-arm sense (lower CI boundary) rather than powered for a randomised superiority comparison
Mixed biological subtypes; benefit estimates in subgroups less precise
Clinical risk defined with a modified Adjuvant! Online tool

clinicalImplications.text: Provides evidence that the 70-gene signature can identify a subset of clinically high-risk patients in whom chemotherapy adds a small absolute benefit in distant metastasis-free survival, supporting shared decision-making about omission.

tumourBoardPearl.text: MINDACT answers 'is it safe enough to skip?' rather than 'is there zero benefit?' — the abstract reports a small absolute difference favouring chemotherapy in the high clinical/low genomic risk group.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 27557300. Long-term updates not yet ingested.
